newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia unveils 10-year industry master plan.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia unveils 10-year industry master plan.

text.p: Malaysia unveiled a 10-year master plan for industry on Thursday which it said will focus on developing eight key sectors up to 2005.

The eight key industrial sectors identified for development were electrical and electronics, textiles and apparel, chemicals, resource-based industries, agro-based and food products industries, transport, materials, and machinery.

Under the new plan, the manufacturing sector is projected to grow 10.7 percent annually up to the year 2000 and slow down to an average of 8.3 percent a year until 2005, said the Ministry of International Trade and Industry, which prepared the plan.
"This relatively lower growth of the manufacturing sector is in line with the optimum growth pattern experienced in most developed economies," the ministry said.
The Second Industrial Master Plan picks up from the where the first plan, effective between 1986-1995, ended.

The manufacturing sector is expected to account for 37.5 percent and 38.4 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2000 and 2005, respectively. Last year, manufacturing contributed 33.1 percent of GDP.
